chain.label: Nitrogen-stabilized hard alpha inclusion in stage 1 fan disk bore
chain.trigger: the fatigue crack initiated in a nitrogen-stabilized type I hard alpha defect at the inside surface of the bore

chain.label: Double-vacuum melt process and manufacturing inspections failed to eliminate or detect the defect
chain.trigger: The hard alpha defect was formed during manufacture of the material and remained undetected through ultrasonic, macroetch, and FPI inspections performed during manufacture of the part.

caused_by.evidence: the vacuum-melt process has not been adequate to produce a defect-free product

chain.label: Cavity created at defect during final machining/shot peening after GEAE inspections
chain.trigger: the cavity was created during the final machining and/or shot peening at the time of GEAE's manufacture of the disk, after GEAE's ultrasonic and macroetch manufacturing inspections

caused_by.evidence: The cavity and surrounding hard alpha material provided a stress raiser from which the fatigue crack initiated.
macroetch was performed on the rectilinear machine forged shape instead of on the final part shape

chain.label: Fatigue crack initiated and grew from the bore defect over the disk's service life
chain.trigger: the hard alpha defect area cracked with the application of stress during the disk's initial exposures to full thrust engine power conditions and that the crack grew

caused_by.evidence: The cavity and surrounding hard alpha material provided a stress raiser from which the fatigue crack initiated.

chain.label: UAL overhaul FPI failed to detect the half-inch fatigue crack 760 cycles before the accident
chain.trigger: the crack was detectable at the time of last inspection with FPI fluid. However, the crack was not detected and consequently the rotor disk was considered to be free of flaws and was accepted as a serviceable part.

caused_by.evidence: the discolored area marks the size of the crack at the time of the last inspection

chain.label: Inadequate human factors consideration in UAL inspection and quality control procedures
chain.trigger: the inadequate consideration given to human factors limitations in the inspection and quality control procedures used by United Airlines' engine overhaul facility

chain.label: Catastrophic separation and uncontained disintegration of No. 2 engine stage 1 fan disk in cruise
chain.trigger: the accident sequence was initiated by a catastrophic separation of the stage 1 fan disk from the No. 2 engine during cruise flight

caused_by.evidence: at the time of the disk separation, the fatigue crack was of a magnitude that would cause fracture and resulting separation of the disk
the failure to detect a fatigue crack originating from a previously undetected metallurgical defect located in a critical area of the stage 1 fan disk
which resulted in the failure to detect a fatigue crack

chain.label: DC-10 hydraulic system protection did not cover the debris pattern and energy of a fan disk burst
chain.trigger: the liberation of debris in a pattern of distribution and with energy levels that exceeded the level of protection provided by design features of the hydraulic systems that operate the DC-10's flight controls

chain.label: Uncontained debris breached all three hydraulic systems, draining fluid to zero
chain.trigger: The separation, fragmentation and forceful discharge of stage 1 fan rotor assembly parts from the No. 2 engine led to the loss of the three hydraulic systems that powered the airplane's flight controls.

caused_by.evidence: the No. 2 engine failure precipitated severe damage that breached the three hydraulic systems

the potential for hydraulic system damage as a result of the effect of random engine debris should have been given more consideration in the original design and certification requirements of the DC-10

chain.label: Total loss of powered flight controls; no manual reversion available
chain.trigger: Approximately 1 minute after the engine failure, the FDR recorded no further powered movement of the flight control surfaces.

caused_by.evidence: leaving the flight control systems inoperative

chain.label: Crew used differential thrust on remaining engines for partial control; airplane unstabilizable
chain.trigger: The flightcrew experienced severe difficulties controlling the airplane and used differential power from the remaining two engines for partial control.

caused_by.evidence: The only means available to fly the airplane was through manipulation of thrust available from the No. 1 and No. 3 engines.

chain.label: Uncontrolled sink rate and right wing drop just before touchdown
chain.trigger: the captain recalled getting a high sink rate alarm from the ground proximity warning system... the right wing dropped rapidly

caused_by.evidence: the damaged DC-10 airplane, although flyable, could not have been successfully landed on a runway with the loss of all hydraulic flight controls

chain.label: Airplane struck runway 22 threshold, cartwheeled and broke up during attempted landing
chain.trigger: First ground contact was made by the right wing tip followed by the right main landing gear. The airplane skidded to the right of the runway and rolled to an inverted position.

caused_by.evidence: which subsequently crashed during an attempted landing at Sioux Gateway Airport
